# Case 212: Calling Convention Macro `#undef`'d After Use

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Verdict** | 🔴 **BREAKING** |
| **Category** | Breaking |
| **Classification** | Rule |
| **Platforms** | Linux |
| **Flags** | ABI break |

| **Source files** | `catalog/cases/case212_calling_convention_macro_undefined_after_use/` |

| **Subject** | [Calling convention and integer-model changes](by-subject/calling-convention-and-integer-model-changes.md) |

**Category:** Calling Convention | **Verdict:** 🔴 BREAKING

## Verdict and consumer impact

`vector_dot` is declared through `MATHLIB_CALL`, and the header `#undef`s
the macro right after the declaration. v1 defines it as
`__attribute__((sysv_abi))`, v2 as `__attribute__((ms_abi))`, so the
arguments move from `rdi`/`rsi`/`rdx` to `rcx`/`rdx`/`r8`. An unchanged old
consumer reads the wrong registers and computes a wrong result.

The macro no longer exists at the end of the translation unit. A reader that
resolves conventions from the final macro table (`-E -dM`) sees no
`MATHLIB_CALL` at all and reports `NO_CHANGE`; that is the defect the
2026-10-11 re-audit found on the CastXML lane.

## Old/new diff

| v1.h | v2.h |
|---|---|
| `#define MATHLIB_CALL __attribute__((sysv_abi))` | `#define MATHLIB_CALL __attribute__((ms_abi))` |
| `MATHLIB_CALL double vector_dot(...);` | same |
| `#undef MATHLIB_CALL` | same |

## abicheck command

```bash
gcc -shared -fPIC -g v1.c -o libv1.so
gcc -shared -fPIC -g v2.c -o libv2.so
abicheck compare libv1.so libv2.so --header old=v1.h --header new=v2.h
```

## Expected abicheck finding

```text
Verdict: BREAKING (exit 4)
  calling_convention_changed  vector_dot: (default) -> ms_abi
```

Same result with the CastXML and the Clang header backend
(`ABICHECK_AST_FRONTEND=castxml|clang`).

## Minimum evidence

`L1` (debug info): a Clang-built library carries the convention in `DW_AT_calling_convention`. GCC emits none, so a GCC build needs the headers (L2), where the macro is read at the declaration.

## Why abicheck catches it

CastXML drops GNU x86-64 conventions from its output, so abicheck re-runs
the same CastXML command with `-E -dD` and reads each declaration's own
preprocessed line, mapped back through the line markers. That line already
has `MATHLIB_CALL` expanded as it was at the declaration, before the
`#undef`. The Clang backend reads the attribute from the function type.

## Runtime failure demonstration

```bash
gcc app.c -L. -l:libv1.so -Wl,-rpath,. -lm -o app && ./app   # 32.0, exit 0
cp libv2.so libv1.so && ./app                                 # wrong result, exit 1
```

## Safe redesign

Keep one convention for the life of an ABI. Scoping a convention macro with `#undef` is fine; changing what it expands to is a break.
